shortDescription: Send a message to an IRC channel or a nick

options.name: channel
options.description: Channel name. One of O(nick_to) or O(channel) needs to be set. When both are set, the message is sent to both of them.

options.name: nick
options.description: Nickname to send the message from. May be shortened, depending on server's NICKLEN setting.

options.name: nick_to
options.description: A list of nicknames to send the message to. One of O(nick_to) or O(channel) needs to be set. When both are defined, the message is sent to both of them.

options.name: part
options.description: Designates whether user should part from channel after sending message or not. Useful for when using a mock bot and not wanting join/parts between messages.

options.name: style
options.description: Text style for the message. Note italic does not work on some clients.

options.name: timeout
options.description: Timeout to use while waiting for successful registration and join messages, this is to prevent an endless loop.

options.name: use_tls
options.description: Designates whether TLS/SSL should be used when connecting to the IRC server. O(use_tls) is available since community.general 8.1.0, before the option was exclusively called O(use_ssl). The latter is now an alias of O(use_tls). B(Note:) for security reasons, you should always set O(use_tls=true) and O(validate_certs=true) whenever possible. The default of this option changed to V(true) in community.general 10.0.0.

options.name: validate_certs
options.description: If set to V(false), the SSL certificates are not validated. This should always be set to V(true). Using V(false) is unsafe and should only be done if the network between between Ansible and the IRC server is known to be safe. B(Note:) for security reasons, you should always set O(use_tls=true) and O(validate_certs=true) whenever possible. The default of this option changed to V(true) in community.general 10.0.0.
